intro_keywords: Start here: the two ideas and every project

project_home_lines.maths: AI-assisted research on eight Erdős problems: a research record and paper for each, Lean 4 proofs of partial results, and Comparator results where they exist.
project_home_lines.quartic: OpenAI's nearly quartic separation between randomized and quantum query complexity, formalised in Lean 4. Each paragraph of the paper links to the Lean declarations it states.
project_home_lines.lean-exposition: Three expositions of OpenAI's full-support theorem for Sherrington–Kirkpatrick spin-glass minimisers. Each passage links to the Lean 4 declarations of OpenAI's proof.
project_home_lines.proof-reader: Contextual Embeddings (PLDI 2026), each sentence linked to the authors' Lean proof, with a declaration dependency graph and the axioms used. Any paper with public Lean code can be added.
project_home_lines.atlas: An index of OpenAI's 719 maths papers in 372 families, with their Lean statement files and the coverage labels outside reviewers such as MathVet and cert-machine assigned.
project_home_lines.formal-verification: Dafny proofs for 16 computations in an 88-component Python research toolkit, compiled to Python, with maps of which components each proof covers.
project_home_lines.funnel: A worked example of turning one Lean proof, a 1968 case of Erdős #257, into a research record, a specialist paper, an exposition and a video.
project_home_lines.narration-ir: An intermediate representation between a narration script and its animation: what each sentence must explain, its source quotations, and picture changes timed to spoken words.
project_home_lines.agent-trace: A local viewer for Claude Code and Codex session logs: every tool call with its output, export of a chosen level of detail to another chat, and an optional MCP server.
project_home_lines.one-checkout: Commits one agent's reviewed Git patch on top of HEAD while other agents' staged and unstaged edits stay in the working tree, including edits to the same files.
project_home_lines.safety-core: Generates AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and Claude Code hooks from one rulebook, so selected rules are enforced before a command runs rather than only written as instructions.
project_home_lines.codemap: A code browser built from docstrings that agents write in a fixed format: a description of every file and links along function calls, readable by people and by coding agents. Not released.
project_home_lines.code-ontology-bridge: Static analysis exports Python functions and call relations to DuckDB with recursive SQL views, so NVIDIA Auto Ontology's text-to-SQL agent can answer questions about a codebase.
project_home_lines.zenith: Experiments on whether a record of missed bugs improves LLM-written unit tests: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's mean fault-detection score rose from 69.2% to 77.0% on 58 held-out HumanEval problems; about half the gain came from timeouts.

about.heading: I'm Will Cook.
paragraphs: I'm an economics undergraduate in Bristol, taking a year out. I'm using it to do mathematics research and build software with AI agents, and to make what the agents produce easier for people to understand.

Every project here follows two ideas. AI models now produce more Lean proofs, papers and code than anyone can read, so I use AI to explain that output at every level of detail, from a two-minute video down to the Lean declaration behind one sentence of a paper. And I build each pipeline so that running it with a newer model gives a better result.

In maths, I've written Lean 4 proofs of partial results on [eight Erdős problems](d=research), including a 1968 case of problem #257, and a Lean formalisation of [OpenAI's nearly quartic gap between randomized and quantum query complexity](p=quartic). I also build websites where clicking a sentence of a paper opens the Lean declarations it states. Samantha Frohlich, one of the authors of Contextual Embeddings, asked me to [make one for her paper](p=proof-reader).

For coding agents, I've built [a viewer](p=agent-trace) for the commands Claude Code and Codex ran, [a way to commit one agent's fix](p=one-checkout) while another agent is still editing the same files, and [Claude Code hooks](p=safety-core) that block commands breaking a written rule. I've also connected Python codebases to [NVIDIA Auto Ontology](p=code-ontology-bridge). I explain each project in a short and a full [video](films), which I script and record and then animate through a pipeline I built.
I don't have a maths degree. I've spent this year learning how to get reliable work out of agents, have Lean check the proofs they write, and explain the results to people who didn't do the work.

I'm looking for a job, internship, fellowship or research collaboration in research engineering, research software, technical demos or developer relations, at an AI lab or a company applying AI to its own field. If you have a problem you think I should work on, [email me](mailto:williamwkcook@gmail.com). If you think one of the videos gets something wrong, I'd like to hear that too.
